claim_verdicts.evidence: options.md: "The Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) or Encapsulation: Scenarios (classes) that depend on configuration settings depend only on the configuration settings that they use." Same principle (depend only on what you use); the lesson's split-into-small-interfaces half follows directly and is outline item 1.

interfaces.md: "A class or struct that implements an interface must provide implementations for all declared members (unless the interface provides a default implementation)." interface.md: "Member bodies in an interface are the *default implementation*." None of IFullNotifier's three members has a body (NotifierIspViolation.cs:7-12 @ stage-1).

Ran: stage-1 NotifierIspViolation.cs with Retry changed to Retry(int orderId, int attempt), dotnet build (SDK 10, net10.0) -> "error CS0535: 'SmsOnlyNotifier' does not implement interface member 'IFullNotifier.Retry(int, int)'". Docs: "must provide an Equals method that matches the interface signature".

git show stage-1:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Design/NotifierIspViolation.cs lines 7-26: three members as stated; Send => Console.WriteLine($"sms about order {orderId}: {subject}"); History => throw new NotSupportedException("this channel keeps no history"); Retry => throw new NotSupportedException("this channel does not retry").

INotifier.cs:5-8 declares only void Send(int orderId, string subject). NotifierBase.cs:5 "public abstract class NotifierBase : INotifier", :18 "protected abstract string Format(int orderId, string subject);", EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier (:21, :27) override only Format.

Ran: static void Use(IFullNotifier n); Use(new SmsNotifier()); against stage-1 sources, dotnet build -> "error CS1503: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'DonHang.Samples.Oop.SmsNotifier' to 'DonHang.Samples.Design.IFullNotifier'". UseSmall(INotifier) with SmsNotifier/EmailNotifier produced no error.
claim_verdicts.source: local build in scratchpad against examples/don-hang @ stage-1

claim_verdicts.evidence: Follows from code: IFullNotifier exposes History() publicly to any holder (interface members without body are implicitly public, interface.md:30) and SmsOnlyNotifier.History throws NotSupportedException (NotifierIspViolation.cs:21-22); nothing in the type tells the caller which implementation it holds.

Design reasoning derived from the ISP definition in claim 1 (per-dependent need, not method count); worded conditionally in the lesson ("fine when every caller and every implementer needs all three"). No factual/version content.

issues.text: Generalises from one class to all SMS channels. The samples' own SmsNotifier (NotifierBase.cs, shown in §5) keeps a history: NotifierBase has `private readonly List<string> sent` and `public IReadOnlyList<string> Sent`, and Send adds every message to it. A reader who opens NotifierBase.cs sees an SMS notifier that does keep history.
issues.quote: but an SMS channel only ever sends: it keeps no history and never resends
issues.fix: Narrow to the class: "but `SmsOnlyNotifier` only ever sends: it keeps no history and never resends." Apply the same narrowing to the q3 correct explanation ("An SMS channel keeps no history and never resends" -> "`SmsOnlyNotifier` keeps no history and never resends") in en and vi.

issues.text: The quoted source comment (line 14) names `SmsNotifier`, a different class that §5 introduces two paragraphs later (derived from NotifierBase, and it does keep a `Sent` list). The prose does not point this out, so the comment reads as describing SmsNotifier. The q4 option-d explanation also leans on this comment ("the class comment says an SMS channel does not keep messages").
issues.quote: // SmsNotifier only ever sends. It still has to answer for History and Retry —
issues.fix: Either add after the first code block: "(The comment's `SmsNotifier` means this class, `SmsOnlyNotifier`.)", or propose via prompt 08 changing the comment to `SmsOnlyNotifier` at the next tag. In q4 d explanation, replace "the class comment says an SMS channel does not keep messages" with "`SmsOnlyNotifier` has no way to keep messages".

issues.text: The question asks which classes must change under each design; "nothing changes" is too broad for the small design, since classes implementing the separate retry interface would change.
issues.quote: With `INotifier`, nothing changes: retries would live in their own interface, implemented only by classes that can really retry.
issues.fix: Replace with: "With `INotifier`, no class that only sends changes: retries would live in their own interface, and only the classes that implement it, the ones that can really retry, must change."
